name: Haldex Generation 4 AWD coupling controller

read_methods.notes: Diagnostics (identification, trouble codes, measuring groups) are KWP2000 over VW TP2.0 at logical address 0x0A on the drivetrain CAN (public OpenHaldex-C6 capture of an 0AY 907 554 C). No public flash read or write procedure, flash layout or MCU is known, so 'obd' stays unknown and no full read is offered. The lock request (Bremse_4 0x2A0) and the unit's status (Allrad_1 0x2C0) are readable passively on the drivetrain CAN (opendbc vw_pq.dbc).

notes: Fourth-generation Haldex coupling controller (J492; coupling codes 0AY / 0BR / 0BY per Dark Side Developments, controller 0BS 907 554 in public part listings for the Passat CC). 0AY 907 554 C identifies as 'Haldex 4Motion' in the public OpenHaldex-C6 capture; 0AY 907 554 F is a different unit OpenHaldex treats as Gen5 (PQ), so identify on the full part number including suffix. Checksum: null - no Gen4 dump was available (none found in the project's dump library) and no public source describes one, so no scheme is claimed; the Gen5 word-sum is not assumed to apply. Pinout: the in-line harness plug as documented by OpenHaldex (single source; its README also mentions a 6-pin 1J0 973 713 plug for other generations) - TO BE CHECKED ON THE CAR before wiring anything. No terminal-30 pin is documented on the Gen1-4 plug.

bench.notes: Terminal 15 on 1, ground 2, K-line 5, Haldex CAN-H 8 / CAN-L 7 (OpenHaldex). Other sources number the Haldex-side CAN pins differently for other connectors - check before wiring.
bench.resistor_notes: Termination of the Haldex CAN segment is not documented; measure the resistance between CAN-H and CAN-L on the unit first.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
